samples.summary: Memory fallback is unreachable when writes fail but reads succeed (e.g. QuotaExceededError), so the preference silently reverts
samples.evidence: `getDateFormat` returns the stored value first (line 41-42) and only consults `memoryFormat` if the read threw or the stored value is absent/junk. The failure mode the new code claims to handle is not only all-or-nothing SecurityError: `localStorage.setItem` also throws QuotaExceededError (full storage / iOS Safari) while `getItem` keeps working. In that case storage still holds the previous valid value (say "relative"), `setDateFormat("exact")` sets `memoryFormat = "exact"`, the write throws and is swallowed, the CHANGE_EVENT fires, subscribers re-read via `getDateFormat`, the read succeeds and returns "relative" — the Settings `Select` snaps back to the old value with no explanation, exactly the outcome the comment on lines 61-64 says the try/catch prevents. A correct fix is to consult `memoryFormat` first (or set it only when the write actually fails and prefer it over the stale stored value). Note the new test masks this: it mocks BOTH `setItem` and `getItem` to throw, so the read-works/write-fails combination is never exercised.

samples.summary: `memoryFormat` overrides absent/junk stored values, contradicting the documented default fallback and making the preference sticky after storage is cleared
samples.evidence: The docstring on line 38 says the preference falls back to the default "on absent/junk values", and the comment on lines 31-33 says `memoryFormat` is "consulted only when `localStorage` is unreadable or unwritable". Neither holds: line 50 returns `memoryFormat ?? DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` on the perfectly healthy path where `getItem` returned `null` or junk. So once `setDateFormat` has run in a session, clearing/overwriting the key from another tab or devtools (which fires `storage`, waking subscribers) makes this tab keep serving the in-memory value instead of the default, and the invariant "storage is the source of truth when storage works" is broken.

samples.summary: Module-level `memoryFormat` is never reset between tests, making the suite order-dependent
samples.evidence: `beforeEach` only does `localStorage.clear()`, but `memoryFormat` is module state that `setDateFormat` mutates and that `getDateFormat` now consults (src line 50). The "falls back to the default on a junk stored value" test (line 26-29) passes only because it happens to run before the tests that call `setDateFormat("exact")`; run it after them (vitest `--shuffle`, or a future reorder/insertion) and `getDateFormat()` returns "exact", failing. The two new tests paper over this with a manual `setDateFormat(DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT)` at the start/end rather than a reset in `beforeEach`, which is fragile and easy to forget for the next test added.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. getDateFormat (date-format-preference.ts:39-51) returns the localStorage value at line 42 and only falls through to memoryFormat at line 50 when the read throws or yields an absent/junk value. setDateFormat (lines 54-67) sets memoryFormat, swallows any setItem throw, then dispatches CHANGE_EVENT. In the realistic write-fails/read-succeeds case (QuotaExceededError on a full store or iOS Safari), storage still holds the previous valid value, so the forced re-read returns the stale value and the in-memory mirror is never consulted, defeating the session-only fallback the comment at lines 61-64 claims to provide. The Settings control is genuinely controlled by this snapshot (settings/page.tsx:26 useDateFormat, line 70 value={dateFormat}, line 71 onValueChange -> setDateFormat) and useDateFormat passes getDateFormat as the useSyncExternalStore snapshot (lines 82-86), so the Select visibly snaps back to the old value. The reviewer's note that the test masks this is also accurate: tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts:58-77 mocks both setItem (59-63) and getItem (64-68) to throw, so the assertion at line 71 only exercises the read-throws branch and the read-works/write-fails combination is never covered. Only two call sites of setDateFormat exist (settings/page.tsx:71 and the tests) and neither checks write success, so no guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. In-lane for Correctness as an inverted-precedence / ineffective-fallback logic bug.

mergedFrom.summary: Unguarded `localStorage.setItem` in `setDateFormat` throws out of the Select's `onValueChange`, so the preference silently fails to apply instead of degrading

finding.summary: Unguarded `localStorage.getItem` in `getDateFormat` is called as the `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot on every render of the documents list and Settings page; a storage SecurityError takes the whole list down
finding.evidence: `getDateFormat()` (line 31-34) does a bare `localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)` and is passed directly as `getSnapshot` to `useSyncExternalStore` (line 56), so it runs on every render of `DateCell` (document-list.tsx:241) and of Settings (page.tsx:26). Accessing `localStorage` throws outright (SecurityError) in Safari private mode, with third‑party/blocked storage, and in sandboxed iframes — the repo already knows this and guards every other such read: `board-grid.ts:220-228` (`try { localStorage.getItem } catch { return DEFAULT }`), `font-recents.ts:23-26`, `analytics.ts:47-53`. Here the throw happens during render, so instead of falling back to `DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` it propagates and blanks the entire document list — the exact failure mode the surrounding date-parsing guards were written to avoid.

verdict.reason: The described unguarded read does not exist. `getDateFormat()` in packages/frontend/src/lib/date-format-preference.ts:39-51 wraps `localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)` in a `try { ... } catch { }` (lines 40-49) and returns `memoryFormat ?? DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` on failure (line 50), with an explanatory comment naming the exact SecurityError/Safari-private-mode/sandboxed-iframe scenario the finding describes. `setDateFormat` is likewise guarded (lines 58-65) and sets the in-memory mirror before writing so the choice still applies without storage. The line numbers cited by the reviewer are wrong: line 31-34 is a doc comment for `memoryFormat`, and line 56 is a comment inside `setDateFormat`; the `useSyncExternalStore` call is at line 83 and passes a correct third `getServerSnapshot` argument returning `DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT`. There is exactly one implementation in the repo (grep for `getDateFormat`/`wafflebase-date-format` finds no duplicate), and tests at packages/frontend/tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts:42-56 and 58-77 mock `Storage.prototype.getItem`/`setItem` to throw and assert the fallback, so the claimed render-time throw cannot occur.
